38 Nucleus P has 144 neutrons and 93 protons. Nucleus P is unstable and undergoes -decay to
form nucleus Q. Nucleus Q then undergoes – decay to form nucleus R.
Nucleus P is represented by point P on the graph.
Which point on the graph represents nucleus R?

hints: Start from point P at proton number 93 and 144 neutrons and track how an alpha particle changes each axis.
Recall that $\alpha$-decay removes $2$ protons and $2$ neutrons, while $\beta^-$-decay converts one neutron into one proton.
Apply the two decays in order P to Q then Q to R and look for the plotted point with proton number 92 and 141 neutrons.
walkthrough: Identify the start: nucleus P has proton number $Z = 93$ and neutron number $N = 144$, as shown by point P.
Apply $\alpha$-decay: an $\alpha$-particle is $2$ protons + $2$ neutrons, so $Z$ falls by 2 and $N$ falls by 2. Nucleus Q has $Z = 93 - 2 = 91$ and $N = 144 - 2 = 142$.
Apply $\beta^-$-decay to Q: one neutron changes to a proton, so $N$ falls by 1 and $Z$ rises by 1. Nucleus R has $Z = 91 + 1 = 92$ and $N = 142 - 1 = 141$.
Read the graph of number of neutrons against proton number: the point at proton number 92 and 141 neutrons is labelled A.

A.explanation: 92 protons and 141 neutrons matches R after the alpha then beta-minus changes.

B.explanation: 91 protons and 142 neutrons is nucleus Q after only the alpha decay, before the beta-minus decay.

C.explanation: 94 protons and 143 neutrons would require an increase in both numbers, which neither decay produces.

D.explanation: 94 protons and 141 neutrons has one proton too many, from adding rather than subtracting 2 protons in alpha decay.
